National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Details of Proceedings
Meeting of 16 Bhadra 2083
Number of Meetings - 43
Today's meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:22 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly commence. Honourable members, names have been registered to speak during the Zero Hour. I now provide time to speak. First, Honourable Member Kamala Panta.
Honourable Ms. Kamala Panta (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, today we are facing a great disaster. But we had alerted the government about this risk even before the disaster arrived. We had repeatedly drawn the government's attention to the issues of floods, landslides, inundation, and preparedness for monsoon-induced disasters. Today's damage has further intensified our concerns. Floods, landslides, inundation, and excessive rainfall are no longer normal events. Due to climate change, such risks are increasing. Therefore, it is time to translate warnings into immediate action, not to ignore them. I strongly urge the government to mobilize all state power for the search and rescue of missing citizens. Those at risk should be immediately moved to safe locations. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.
Honourable Ms. Jayanti Devi Rai (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, we are in a time of great sorrow. As we all know, the flood in the Bhote Koshi has caused immense loss of life and property, which is immeasurable. It is extremely difficult to save those who have survived. Reaching relief is also very challenging due to the lack of roads, bridges, electricity, and telephone services. Among them, children, the elderly, and the sick are facing even greater difficulties. Therefore, I want to draw the government's attention to finding alternatives. Furthermore, thousands of citizens who were rescued and sent from there, and those who fled on their own, have entered Kathmandu and are residing in various holding centers, monasteries, and temples. It is essential for the government and all helpers to pay attention to them as well.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
Honourable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, I offer my heartfelt condolences to those who died in the unimaginable flood and landslide in Bhote Koshi. I want to demand from the government the immediate search for the families of the missing. The government has stated a one-door system for relief in the event of such an unimaginable incident in the country. A one-door system in times of disaster further burdens people. Therefore, I request strict monitoring to ensure the smooth delivery of relief. And I also want to appeal to the government: when the entire nation is in mourning, what can be said if the state managers themselves lack such sensitivity? Therefore, I again (..time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.
Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, sad and distressing news. The flood in the Bhote Koshi, unseen in this country so far, has made thousands of people disappear. Heartfelt condolences to the deceased and wishes for their eternal peace. People who have not been in contact for 15 days should be declared dead. A survey has counted 3,624 small and large glacial lakes in the northern Himalayas. Of these, 24 are at risk, and 7 are said to be at high risk. Due to the increasing global temperature, glaciers are at greater risk. Therefore, although we cannot do much with nature, roads should be constructed only above 300 meters from the surface of our rivers originating from the Himalayas, and buildings should be constructed only above 500 meters. On one hand, there is the pain of losing relatives and property, and on top of that, due to the negligence in relief and rescue, the affected public (..time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar.
Honourable Mr. Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, the country and its people are writhing in pain and are afflicted. Why was the Prime Minister's visit to Mustang before this? The desire to reach Mustang by road without the flow of continuous rain and landslides has been fulfilled. The history of the tourist paradise of Thang, the meeting with the Mustang king. That geography has history within it, borders, social sensitivities, and is also a study of political memory. The public's suspicion is arising about whether this is a study of a high-altitude base camp for uranium mining, along with the government's behavior, the security apparatus, and foreign powers' interests. What is this? The Prime Minister (..time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
Honourable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, we are suffering from a poison we haven't consumed. We are forced to face destruction from the development of others. The country is crying today from the pain of the great flood in the Bhote Koshi on Bhadra 10th. More than 900 people have died in the devastating flood, and thousands are missing. More than 17,000 children are affected, and many have become orphaned. Billions of rupees worth of physical damage has occurred. We stand with the government in this great calamity. I demand that search, rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction be carried out in coordination with the federal and local governments during this national disaster. I offer my heartfelt condolences to all those who lost their precious lives in the flood, sympathy to their families, and wish for the speedy recovery of the injured. Girls and adolescents staying in sectors are at risk of violence (..recorded audio broken). I demand that a day of national mourning be declared by lowering the national flag. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, the unimaginable loss of life and property caused by the flood in the Bhote Koshi has shocked the world. This can also be understood as the beginning of a vicious cycle created by human interference with nature, including climate change. In this regard, the government's attention is needed to make Nepal's weak early warning system state-of-the-art and better. Honourable Chairperson, what should not have happened has happened. Now the government's attention should be focused on search, rescue, relief, and rehabilitation. Effective action and inclusive management are necessary, otherwise, there is a danger of another crisis in the form of an epidemic. Through you, Honourable Chairperson, I urge the government to declare Bhadra 10th as a National Mourning Day. Finally, I express my heartfelt condolences to the citizens who lost their lives in the flood. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rajendra Lakshmi Gaire.
Honourable Ms. Rajendra Lakshmi Gaire (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, the flood on Bhadra 10th has turned the happiness and dreams of many families in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading into debris. Many families may be buried inside their homes. Relatives are wandering in search of the living and the dead. There is still an assessment that there are living people in the debris, and if they find living people, they will embrace them with joy; if they find bodies, they will console themselves by crying. If neither is found, people's minds will be disturbed. Therefore, I want to draw the government's attention to pay more attention, even though it is already paying some attention. It has been reported that attention has not been paid to epidemics after the disaster, and to medicines for children, women, and the chronically ill. Please pay attention.
Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, the previous honourable members have already shed light on the loss of life and property caused by the sudden devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi river and related facts and figures. I agree with that. (..recorded audio broken) and along with wishing for the speedy treatment of the injured, I want to demand from the government to expedite the rescue and relief work. In this regard, Honourable Chairperson, I also want to say that there is a role of rich and highly developed countries behind this natural disaster. Due to the environmental imbalance they have created in the context of development, such natural disasters and calamities are occurring. We are bearing the consequences of this. I want to draw the international community's attention to this and demand that a country like Nepal should receive compensation for it. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa.
Honourable Mr. Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party (UML)):- Honourable Chairperson, I express my deep sorrow over the loss of life and property in areas including Rasuwa, Dhading, and Nuwakot due to the flood caused by the avalanche on Bhadra 10, 2082. I express my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. In this hour of grief, all citizens need to unite for relief and rescue. I draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to quickly provide relief and rescue by ascertaining the exact details of the currently missing persons. I express my heartfelt gratitude to all the rescuers, organizations, and the Government of Nepal for the ongoing rescue efforts. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the turn to speak during the Zero Hour concludes here. Honourable members, I will sequentially provide time to honourable members to speak on behalf of the parties represented in the National Assembly. Time is 7 minutes. First, Honourable Member Kamala Panta.
Honourable Ms. Kamala Panta (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, I offer my heartfelt condolences to all the citizens who lost their lives in the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi river on Bhadra 10th and other natural disasters. I express my heartfelt sympathy to the families who are in grief and pain after losing their loved ones. We express our deep solidarity with the families anxious about the search for their still missing relatives. We also state that in this difficult time, the state's presence should be seen not on paper, but at the doorstep of the victims.
Chairperson, the disaster that started in the Bhote Koshi region of Rasuwa has caused serious damage to settlements and important infrastructure in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and even Gorkha, including Timure, Syabrubesi, Betrawati, and Trishuli. The operation of trade routes and the Syabrubesi port has also been affected. With the disruption of road, communication, and electricity services, the daily life of citizens has been severely impacted. The first priority now is to save lives. There should be no delay in the search, rescue, and relief of missing citizens. Especially in the case of workers and technicians trapped inside the tunnels of hydropower projects, normal rescue efforts are insufficient. A special rescue team with modern tunnel rescue technology, skilled manpower, and necessary equipment should be deployed immediately.
Honourable Chairperson, I do not want to say anything bad or unpleasant now. But the government...

It has also been reported that it has been washed away. In such an irresponsible manner, the public cannot get any relief from this disaster. Road connectivity has been cut off. In the affected areas, if land routes are not possible, food grains, medicines, temporary shelter materials, and health workers must be delivered by air rescue and transport. Although information has come that it has reached some places, the government must understand that the life of every citizen matters. Local governments, provincial governments, and local representatives of the people in the Terai and local levels exist, but it is heard that there is no coordination. If the government proceeds in this manner, we will not be able to escape the problem. Similarly, human sensitivity is extremely important in the identification and management of the bodies found. Let the bodies be identified through DNA and fingerprint technology as needed and handed over to relatives without administrative hassle. In the case of unidentified bodies, arrangements should be made for dignified cremation respecting the customs, culture, and traditions of the concerned religion. It is being heard now that bodies have even reached India. What is the status of this? Respected Chairperson, I demand with the seriousness of the government that we should get information from the parliament, not from social media, about the current situation. We should get information from the government in the parliament.

Need for national cooperation. Today is not the time for political competition. Today is the time to demonstrate national unity, cooperation, and human sensitivity. Facing such a great natural disaster cannot be achieved by the efforts of one ministry, one level of government, or one political party alone. However, it is heard that an individual has gone and distributed relief through an unknown organization, and if this is true, we cannot accept it. The joint effort of the federal, provincial, and local governments, security agencies, the private sector, non-governmental organizations, civil society, the government sector, and the general public is necessary.

Respected Chairperson, a technical team should be deployed immediately. The government should be active not after the risk is confirmed, but as soon as the possibility of risk is seen. Now, the situation of potential risk areas should be assessed, local citizens should be given prior notice, and if necessary, they should be transferred to safe places for future disasters. Chairperson, the reconstruction from now on should not be about rebuilding where it was destroyed, but about rebuilding where citizens are safe. It is not about rebuilding roads where they are repeatedly destroyed.

Chairperson, we are experiencing the effects of climate change. This climate change has put the country at risk, the entire country. We are talking about reservoirs from glaciers originating from the Himalayas. We call ourselves a country of rivers, but this is causing us disaster. Today is not the time for political competition, today is the time to save lives.

Respected Chairperson, without speaking at length, every minute is important in the hour of natural disaster. I urge the government and all concerned bodies to conduct a swift search and safe rescue of missing citizens. Let us move beyond political differences and advance national cooperation.

Chairperson, I request the government to provide complete information regarding the situation, as I have already said, and we need air, we need bodies, we need food, we need shelter, and the state must also provide hope. Now, after the disaster strikes, the government should be visible before the pre-warning, not after searching for it. Decisions should be made not after the settlement is washed away, but when the risk is seen. The state must be active beforehand to save lives, not after lives are lost.

Chairperson, today some families are searching for their loved ones, some citizens are waiting for relief, some settlements are cut off from road and communication contact, and many families are still hoping for the return of their missing relatives. I have visited many families saying they will return, and they are waiting. Thank you.

Respected Chairperson: Honorable Member Jhakk Prasad Subedi.
(13:41 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Jhakk Prasad Subedi (Nepal Communist Party):- Respected Chairperson
(13:42 hrs)
Sir, on the morning of August 10th, a terrible destructive flood from Tibet at the Rasuwagadhi Timure customs point caused unimaginable loss of life and property. Nepal and Nepalis have faced a cruel and heartbreaking disaster that has never been experienced or seen in history. This event is unimaginable not only in Nepal but also in the eyes of the world. Our National Assembly member Shri Shree Krishna Adhikari's brother Badri Adhikari also lost his life there in this unfortunate and heartbreaking incident. I offer my heartfelt condolences to him and all those who lost their lives in this unfortunate and heartbreaking incident. I express deep sympathy to the bereaved families and solidarity with the relatives of those whose loved ones are missing.

Sir, Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, and Chitwan were most affected by this heartbreaking incident. Not only this, but it has affected the entire Nepal and the world. Citizens from more than two dozen districts including Rolpa, Salyan, Jajarkot, Nawalparasi, Sindhupalchok, Dolakha, Ramechhap, Sindhuli, Rautahat, Udaypur have been affected by this disaster and are still missing. This disaster is not just about dozens of districts within the country; hundreds of foreign tourists from dozens of countries including China and India have gone missing in this disaster. This disaster can only be faced by establishing national unity with the commitment, initiative, and collective activism of the government, all political parties, and civil society, rising above party lines. Thousands of pilgrims and tourists, as well as laborers from flood-affected areas and across the country who went there for employment, have also lost their lives. The government's first responsibility is to rescue the living as much as possible, and this is the government's primary duty. The second duty is to hand over the bodies of those not found alive to their families. Third, to arrange for the proper treatment of the injured as soon as possible and to distribute immediate relief to the survivors. After that, to engage in rehabilitation and reconstruction work.

Nepal and Nepalis have faced a heartbreaking disaster that has never been experienced in history. This has become unimaginable not only in Nepal but also in the eyes of the world. Honorable Members of the National Assembly, Honorable Kiran Babu Shrestha and I, just yesterday, participated in a seminar organized by the IPU in China. Two honorable members of the House of Representatives are arriving today. The seminar also seriously discussed the irreparable loss of life and property caused by the BhoteKoshi flood in Nepal. We seriously raised the issue from our side that the consequences of the exploitation of nature by developed and developing countries due to climate change are what we are experiencing. Currently, the Nepal Army, Armed Police Force, and Nepal Police are working according to their capabilities, but even so, rescue operations are still delayed in many places. Newborns, women, girls, elderly citizens, disabled persons, and children are being kept with other adult men. They should not be kept like that. The government should make proper arrangements for newborns, girls, women, elderly citizens, children, and the disabled. In Rasuwa, the police informed about the flood and worked to save the citizens, but those police themselves were swept away by the muddy flood. Chairperson, we have received information that the Armed Police Force and District Police are currently without resources. Home Minister, do not just sit in the tunnel; the government's job, and especially the Home Minister's job, is to coordinate with the security forces, cooperate with foreign organizations, and make relief materials effective. Prioritize the treatment of the injured and make good arrangements for the homeless. Although the government is much discussed on social media and in the news, the government's presence in the field appears weak. Chairperson, there are three types of governments in the country, but we have received information that the federal government is treating the provincial and local governments like the opposition party. The federal government should not do that. Various political parties and citizens from all over the country directly assisted the victims of the earthquake, COVID, and floods in the Madhesh. We ourselves went there, but it is everyone's duty to visit the victims and provide direct assistance, and everyone should receive it. Finally, national unity is the reliable basis for overcoming this great disaster. The government should take this matter seriously. Thank you.

Respected Chairperson: Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dangal.
(13:48 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dangal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):-
Respected
(13:49 hrs)
Sir, the country is in mourning at this time. We are extremely saddened, extremely distressed. How cruel is fate! In an instant, a catastrophic flood challenged human civilization itself. Yes, on August 10, 2083, a devastating and terrible flood from Tibet in the Xizang Autonomous Region of China caused a large number of human and physical casualties in districts like Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading. Thousands of citizens have died in the flood.
The number of missing persons is large, and the number of injured is also large. First of all, I want to offer my heartfelt condolences to all the mothers, fathers, brothers, and sisters who have died in this devastating flood. Similarly, I express deep sympathy to all the bereaved families who have lost their loved ones. Respected Chairperson, I also wish for the speedy recovery of all the injured. I want to state that we stand with the flood-affected communities in this hour of irreparable loss of life and property suffered by the country.

The first responsibility of the state is to protect the lives of citizens affected by the disaster. Therefore, even though it is very late, the state should complete this work at a war footing to save citizens' lives and search for the missing. I request this. The bodies of citizens who have died so far are scattered along the riverbanks. It is necessary to work diligently to collect those bodies and identify them and hand them over to their relatives. I draw attention to this. Similarly, there are a large number of workers waiting for rescue in the tunnels of various hydropower projects, so the state's immediate attention is also necessary in this regard, and those workers need to be rescued. Similarly, by taking all political parties, organizations, and civil society along, I suggest to the government that this challenge can be faced by establishing national unity at such a time and doing so. Similarly, I request that the work of rescue, search, and relief be carried forward at a war footing. Relief distribution is very delayed. Former honorable members have also mentioned this. I draw the state's attention to speed up this work even more. There is a widespread complaint that coordination between governments at all levels is not good. Therefore, I heartily request to face this challenge by establishing close coordination between the federal, provincial, and local governments. The work we will do after this is Post-Disaster Need Assessment (PDNA). By doing this, after the disaster...

and to assess the damage and loss and identify the needs, build infrastructure, and then resettle the displaced communities. This work needs to start now. Therefore, it is necessary to ascertain accurate facts, especially regarding the extent of the damage, the loss incurred, and our needs for reconstruction and resettlement. Similarly, in carrying out reconstruction, we need to work according to the 'Build Back Better' (BBB) concept. This means we need to carry out reconstruction work that is better, stronger, and more durable than before. Likewise, I would like to earnestly request that resettlement be done by constructing integrated settlements for displaced families to ensure their safety from future disasters. I demand that the agricultural land damaged by the floods be reclaimed, developed, made suitable for cultivation, and farmers be resettled. This disaster is due to climate change. Our country has a very minimal role in climate change. Specifically, developed countries, industrial countries, and some developing countries, emerging countries, have caused the Earth to warm by extensively using fossil fuels to operate their industries and infrastructure, by operating transportation, and by conducting development activities, releasing large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Due to industrialization, methane gas has also been emitted in large quantities in the name of agricultural industrialization, using chemicals, leading to a situation where greenhouse gases are accumulating. Therefore, I believe that these developed countries are responsible for this disaster. We must receive compensation from the Green Climate Fund for climate justice. The Government of Nepal needs to raise this issue strongly at the international level. Just as a cabinet meeting was held at Kalapatthar before the Copenhagen Accord in 2009, similarly, our glaciers are melting, and we have suffered great losses; this needs to be internationalized, and we need to receive justice accordingly. Finally, developed countries must reduce greenhouse gas emissions to the extent they are emitting them. It is unjust for them to continue emitting gas while we bear the brunt. We absolutely do not want to tolerate this. This is climate injustice, and therefore, to protect this Earth and human civilization, it is necessary to adopt the concept of sustainable development for climate justice. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mr. Mahanta Thakur. Please come here, it will be more convenient there. (13:56 hrs) It will be convenient for the honorable member there, and there is also permission to speak there. Honorable Mr. Mahanta Thakur (Democratic Socialist Party, Nepal): (13:57 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, today, regarding the flood in Bhote Koshi, the damage that has occurred, I would like to offer condolences for that damage. Lives have been lost, property has been lost, families have been lost, people are missing, and even bodies have been found across the border. This is a great disaster for us. Whether it is called man-made or a natural disaster, it is a gift of nature. Therefore, it has united the entire country, everyone, in the bond of unity, and it also reminds us that we can do many things with our own strength and that we are ready and prepared for it. Our neighbors have also helped us. Those living abroad are also connected to our motherland, the youth are all connected, and in this way, wherever we are, inside or outside, we are all united in this disaster, and we all who have suffered, on behalf of myself and on behalf of all of you. Everyone knows that whoever dies, this is the tribute. We are also mortal. I offer tribute from my side to those who have passed away, and I express heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. I will conclude my brief remarks here. Thank you. (14:00 hrs) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, the turn of honorable members to speak on behalf of the parties concludes here. Honorable Members, Nepal is a country at high risk of various natural and human-induced disasters, including floods, landslides, earthquakes, fires, and epidemics. Although Nepal's contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions is very low, it is a fact before us all that Nepal is at the forefront among countries experiencing the adverse effects of climate change. In this context, the sudden and devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa on Bhadra 10, 2083 BS, which caused significant human and physical damage in coastal areas and riverbanks in districts such as Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan, has deeply concerned and saddened the National Assembly. The actual details of the damage caused by this disaster have not yet been fully ascertained. According to information received from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority as of 9:00 AM on Bhadra 16, 1,814 people have been rescued, and 3,916 are missing. Search and rescue operations are ongoing, and the actual details of the deceased, missing, injured, and physical damage are being updated and verified. The National Assembly offers its heartfelt condolences to the Nepali citizens and citizens of various countries who lost their lives in this tragic incident. I express deep sympathy to their bereaved families, relatives, and concerned nations and communities. I also wish for the safe return of the missing domestic and foreign citizens. Honorable Members, on behalf of the National Assembly, I express heartfelt thanks to the relevant bodies of the Government of Nepal, the Nepali Army, Nepal Police, Armed Police Force Nepal, local administration, media, local governments, health workers, Red Cross, volunteers, journalists, local communities, and all rescuers who were directly or indirectly involved in search, rescue, treatment, relief, and humanitarian assistance during this time of disaster, risking their own lives. The National Assembly also expresses its heartfelt gratitude for the technical expertise, relief, assistance, and solidarity received from friendly nations and the international community in this humanitarian rescue operation. I also express my belief that the federal, provincial, and local governments will effectively fulfill their respective responsibilities in this disaster situation and work in an integrated and coordinated manner in accordance with the spirit of federalism and the concept of cooperation and coordination envisioned by the constitution. I especially express my heartfelt thanks for the specialized technical and expert assistance provided for the search and rescue of individuals trapped in risky and difficult terrain, river areas, tunnels, and various structures, as well as for the specialized forensic and DNA-related assistance provided for the identification and scientific management of bodies. In view of the seriousness of this disaster, I draw the serious attention of the Government of Nepal and all concerned bodies to arrange for the prompt and free treatment of the injured, prioritize the search and rescue of missing citizens, and maximize the utilization of all available resources, means, technology, and manpower. I also urge that arrangements be made to effectively transfer citizens in risky areas, such as riverbanks and other hazardous locations, to safe places, ensure easy access to health services and essential goods, and provide regular and reliable information flow in the affected areas. It is necessary to ensure transparency, orderliness, and needs-based management of the collection, storage, transportation, and distribution of relief materials, ensuring that relief reaches the actual affected citizens in a timely manner. I also draw the attention of the concerned bodies to immediately address any problems or public grievances observed during the distribution of relief. Similarly, I urge that the bodies concerned manage the bodies of those who lost their lives in the disaster in a dignified, safe, and scientific manner and use appropriate scientific methods and technologies for the identification of unidentified bodies. Honorable Members, the damage from this disaster is not limited to the immediate humanitarian aspect. It has also severely affected housing, roads, bridges, electricity, communication, drinking water, irrigation, education, health services, and other essential infrastructure. Therefore, I also urge that the actual physical and sectoral assessment of the damage be carried out promptly through processes such as 'Post Disaster Needs Assessment' and that a clear action plan for relief, rehabilitation, reconstruction, and compensation be developed based on it. Given that the nature and impact of the disaster transcend administrative boundaries, it is necessary to further strengthen coordination and cooperation among the federal, provincial, and local governments, including information exchange, resource mobilization, and clear responsibilities, to advance rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction efforts in an integrated manner. In addition, I draw the government's attention to establishing national unity with a concrete plan, rising above party politics, to fight against national disasters. Honorable Members, this disaster has become a shared global issue of human sensitivity, not just for Nepal. In this context, while addressing the Second Inter-Parliamentary Speakers' Conference held in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, a few days ago, I seriously raised the issue of the significant human and physical damage caused by the devastating flood in Nepal to the international community. Through that international forum, I also made a heartfelt appeal for humanitarian assistance and solidarity for rescue, relief, and rehabilitation to the United Nations and the entire international community. Furthermore, raising the issue that countries like Nepal, with a low role in climate change, are suffering more from disasters created by others, I have appealed to the parliaments of the world and the international community to arrange for a special international fund for such affected countries and to extend support. The National Assembly expresses its heartfelt gratitude to all friendly nations, the United Nations, international organizations, development partners, and the community of supporters for this solidarity, goodwill, and cooperation extended to Nepal. I also once again earnestly appeal on behalf of the National Assembly to friendly nations, international organizations, and supporting bodies interested in providing necessary assistance for rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction in the coming days to coordinate with the Government of Nepal and provide needs-based assistance. I also urge all honorable members of the National Assembly to deposit at least 15 days' salary into the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund and the Prime Minister's Relief Fund as per their convenience. I also urge the concerned parties to ensure transparency and effective utilization of the received assistance. Honorable Members, this incident has reminded us once again that it is not enough to focus only on rescue and relief after a disaster strikes. It is necessary to effectively implement risk identification, preparedness, early warning, and risk reduction measures even before a disaster occurs. Especially in the Himalayan and riverine areas, the expansion and strengthening of the early warning system, the mechanism for inter-country information exchange

management, risk mapping, safe settlement development, disaster-resilient infrastructure construction, and enhancing community's disaster response capacity through timely and long-term strategies. I also draw attention to the need for prompt restoration and reconstruction of essential infrastructure damaged by floods and landslides, such as roads, bridges, electricity, sanitation, and health facilities, and to consider future disaster risks during reconstruction. I would also like to remind everyone that the National Assembly is a common institution of representatives with a history of believing in the rule of law and constitutional processes. Therefore, it will always remain vigilant against any attempts to undermine laws, processes, the constitution, acts, and regulations, and will strongly oppose such activities. Finally, I appeal to the general public residing in riverine and risk-prone areas during this sensitive time to exercise extreme caution, avoid unnecessary travel, fully comply with advance warnings and safety directives issued by relevant bodies, and immediately move to safe locations if a risk is observed. I also request everyone not to disseminate unverified information, rumors, or misleading messages regarding disasters and to participate in relief and assistance efforts only through official and reliable channels. Disaster management is a shared responsibility of the federal and local governments, security agencies, civil society, the private sector, communities, friendly nations, international partners, and the general public. I make a special appeal to all political parties, their affiliated organizations, social organizations, civil society, entrepreneurs, businesspersons, and government employees to unite in this difficult time and advance life protection, search and rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction efforts effectively, transparently, and humanely. I also seriously draw the attention of the Nepal government to move forward with a concrete plan to unite all parties and protect the lives and property of the people. Thank you. Honorable members, I now present a special motion regarding the unprecedented disaster. Honorable members, on the occasion of the tragic loss of life and property due to the devastating flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa on August 26, 2026, I express heartfelt condolences to those who lost their lives and deep sympathy to their bereaved families. I urge the Nepal government to pay special attention to coordinating between different levels of government for the rescue, relief, and rehabilitation of flood-affected individuals, the search for the missing, free treatment for the injured, scientific management of corpses, and reconstruction of physical infrastructure. I also urge for the establishment of national unity through the cooperation and coordination of local communities, civil society, the private sector, development partners, and international communities to manage disasters and adopt effective measures to reduce future disaster risks. I request that this special motion be passed. Honorable members, I declare the motion unanimously passed. Honorable members, I now provide the floor to the Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honorable Prime Minister, to present the annual report of the National Dalit Commission for the fiscal year 2080/081. Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam: (14:93 PM) With the permission of the Honorable Chairperson, I present the annual report of the National Dalit Commission for the fiscal year 2080/081 to this esteemed assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on August 29, 2026, at 1:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned. (Subsequently, the meeting was adjourned until the next meeting on August 29, 2026, at 1:15 PM.) Adjournment: 14:15 PM.
